rationale: The route (REACTION→USER→CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→CONVERSATION→WORKSPACE) correctly implements the prompt's disambiguation of 'Robert' via core-infra conversation membership, distinct from the message's actual channel (product-growth), matching the binding_note's explicit statement that the reacted-on message need not sit in core-infra. Seed data genuinely supports the disambiguation: Robert Walsh (channel_members rows for general/random/engineering) lacks a core-infra row, while Robert Chen has one, and Kenji's Tokyo stats message exists verbatim in the base seed at the cited timestamp in C_GROWTH. The four required message_reactions rows are plan-stage additions (permitted per instructions) and jointly produce a clean single match with three well-motivated negatives: same-message-wrong-Robert (channel filter fails), same-channel-wrong-name (name filter fails), and same-person-wrong-message (message binding fails), each isolating a distinct edge of the route. Answer attribute is a bare column (message_reactions.reaction_type), access plan uses visible/known channel and team IDs consistent with the stated scope_exception (no workspace-name lookup), and resolution_mode single is justified since exactly one qualifying reaction exists. No mechanical or access defects found; the one minor point (only one workspace exists in seed, making the WORKSPACE node's bounding role somewhat trivial) is a quality nuance, not a validity defect, and the design otherwise reads as an ordinary, well-motivated case with useful path-derived negatives.
